texts: On day 16 of Year 1, a cold wind blew off the sea at night.
The cold wind was a north wind.
The cold wind struck the Cliff Path at night.
The cold wind came before the first hard frost.
The salt-bloom season had not yet started.
The keepers on the Cliff Path had not yet added salt-bloom to the mire-essence of their lanterns.
That night, eleven lanterns on the Middle Row were unprepared.
The eleven lanterns went out before dawn.
No lantern at the Sunken Cove went out.
No lantern in the Northcove went out.
The cliff-spires sheltered the Northcove against the north wind.

q1_issues.issue: "The cold wind WAS a north wind" is a past-tense copular, so the categorical atom must be wrapped as (Past (Member sk_wind_1 north_wind)); the surface tense decides mechanically.
The past tense of "were unprepared" is dropped entirely — the reified per-member state carries Time atoms but no (Past ...).

A copular clause with a time modifier must dual-emit the flat copular atom beside the reified state (for a group, as the per-member flat rule over (PartOf $x sk_lanterns_2)); only the reified half is present, so "is this lantern unprepared?" cannot bind.

"The keepers ... had not yet added" is a definite plural with a distributive predicate, so the negated clause should emit the per-member distribution rule at strength 0.0 as well, not the group-level denial alone.

q2_gaps: a passage-initial date frame ("On day 16 of Year 1, ...") whose scope carries over later sentences — the instruction set covers anaphoric temporal NPs ("that night") but not frame persistence, so the striking and coming events keep only the day-part and lose the date
review.notes: The two past-perfect denials (statements 30, 40) leave their anteriority to the night's events unencoded because the ordering test is stated over "the sentence", which gives a multi-sentence passage no carrier for it. Role choices (Patient for the wind's blowing/coming, Agent for the transitive striking and sheltering), the go_out phrasal verb, the "no lantern" rules with their QuantifierPhrase companions, and the On/Against surface-preposition heads all follow the instruction set.

issues.reason: Status predicates states that tense over a copular clause wraps the categorical atom and that "the surface tense decides, mechanically" ("Alice was happy" -> (Past (Member alice happy))), so the bare (Member sk_wind_1 north_wind) drops the stated past tense of "was a north wind".

The copular-with-time-modifier example is explicit that the reified state carries the tense — "Alice was ill on Friday" -> ... (Time sk_ill_1 (Weekday friday)) (Past sk_ill_1) — and Reciprocals requires any status to sit inside a rule's consequent, so the conclusion needs (Past (sk_unprepared $x)); "were unprepared" loses its tense entirely.

Core patterns lists "a copular clause carrying a time modifier" as a dual-emit, and Resultatives fixes the group case — the flat half becomes the per-member rule (Implication (PartOf $x <group>) (Member $x <state>)) — so emitting only the reified-state rule drops a mandated half.

Negation (events) states that a negated plural or group "keeps both emissions" — the group denial AND the distribution rule, each at strength 0.0, "dropping either is a different, weaker claim" — and "add" is not one of the collective predicates (gather/meet/assemble/collide), as the parse itself recognizes for the go_out clause at lines 50-53.

gaps_confirmed: A passage-initial date frame ("On day 16 of Year 1, ...") whose scope runs on over later sentences has no carrier — term propagation covers only anaphoric temporal NPs, so "struck the Cliff Path at night" and the coming/frost clauses keep the day-part and lose the date (the parse correctly propagates only at "That night").
new_gaps: An epoch-style calendar reference ("day 16 of Year 1") has no Time term distinct from the Gregorian day-of-month: (Day 16) occupies the day-of-month slot with no Month to anchor it, so a day-of-year index and a month-day are indistinguishable downstream.

A past perfect whose anteriority is to the NARRATIVE reference time rather than to a specific asserted event has no licensed ordering: "had not yet started" / "had not yet added" precede the night of day 16, not any one event in the text, and the Before test needs "another asserted event" to order against — worse, both perfects sit inside strength-0 denials, so there is no positive eventuality to put in Before's slot at all.

An aspectual particle on a NEGATED PLURAL clause has no licensed place once the per-member distribution rule is added: (Yet e) must be a positive atom outside the strength-0 bundle, but inside a strength-0 rule's conclusion it would be denied, and Reciprocals forbids a free-variable atom outside the rule — so the per-member half of "had not yet added" cannot carry its "yet".
adjudication.defect_summary: Issue 0: the compliant form is (Past (Member sk_wind_1 north_wind)), the decomposition atoms staying unwrapped as definitional. Issue 1: the rule's conclusion must add (Past (sk_unprepared $x)) beside its Member/Experiencer/Time conjuncts. Issue 2: the flat half must be emitted as the per-member rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_lanterns_2) (Past (Member $x unprepared))) (STV 1.0 0.9), beside the reified-state rule. Issue 3: the group denial must be joined by (Implication (PartOf $x sk_keepers_1) (And (Member (sk_add $x) add) (Agent (sk_add $x) $x) (Theme (sk_add $x) salt_bloom) (Goal (sk_add $x) sk_mire_essence_1) (Past (sk_add $x)))) (STV 0.0 0.9) — but its "yet" then has no licensed carrier (filed as a new gap).
adjudication.notes: Role choices, the go_out phrasal verb kept whole, the entity-attached On/Against heads, the "no lantern" strength-0 rules with their QuantifierPhrase companions, the Ordinal on the first hard frost, and the TimeAtMost dawn bound all follow the instruction set. The parse emits the group-plus-per-member pair correctly for "the eleven lanterns went out", which is what makes its absence at "had not yet added" an inconsistency rather than a reading choice.
